newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ex-E.German official's smuggling conviction upheld.
newsitem.headline: Ex-E.German official's smuggling conviction upheld.

text.p: The German Federal Court of Justice on Wednesday upheld a 1996 conviction of former East Berlin secret police colonel Alexander Schalck-Golodkowski for smuggling arms into communist East Germany.

Schalck-Golodkowski, whose shadowy hard currency deals kept the former German Democratic Republic afloat, had appealed against his conviction for illegally importing guns and night-vision devices worth 8.5 million marks ($5.5 million) during the Cold War.
A lower Berlin court sentenced him to an 18-month suspended jail sentence and Schalck-Golodkowski appealed against the verdict.

His lawyers had argued in court that as a former East German citizen, he could not be convicted of breaking a Cold War law promulgated by Western victor powers which lapsed with unification in 1990. They asked if East Germany could be expected to respect an arms embargo against itself.

Schalck-Golodkowski inhabited a twilight world between the capitalist and communist spheres, heading a scarcely penetrable web of Western firms and contacts as head of East Berlin's shadowy Commercial Coordination (KoKo) department.

KoKo's main task was to rake in the billions of marks of hard currency which for years kept the ailing regime afloat. But it also existed to procure all the things East Germany most wanted, ranging from hi-tech goods to Western entertainment videos and luxury items for East Berlin's ageing rulers.
